notes: Library is the best-supplied arena in the game: three armours, the most ammunition by a wide margin and eight spawn points. That abundance is its defining property -- attrition strategies fail here because nobody stays starved.
See mp/_general.json for the cross-arena layer.

nuance.claim: Denying supplies does not work here, because there is far too much of everything; matches are decided by fighting rather than by starving an opponent out.
nuance.because: Library carries three Armour records and thirty-one AmmoBox records, nearly three times Basement's eleven.

nuance.claim: Three armours spread across the floors mean no single one can be held usefully; the map is played as a rotation.
nuance.because: Library carries three Armour records, tied with Complex for the most.

nuance.claim: With the joint-most spawn points in the game, spawn denial is not a workable plan here and effort is better spent holding routes than reappearance points.
nuance.because: Library carries eight Spawn records, the joint most of any arena.

nuance.claim: The whole map reduces to knowing where each level connects to the next; a player who knows the entrances and exits between floors controls the pace of every fight.
The lower area is tighter and more enclosed, which makes it the reliable place to break pursuit; running along an upper floor keeps you visible.
The open upper areas give long sightlines in several directions at once, so they are strong to hold and dangerous to cross.
Breakable glass means several apparent walls are not, so cover has to be judged by what is behind it rather than by what looks solid.
Movement between areas passes through a limited set of doorways, which are where engagements should be sought and mines should be placed.
The shelving splits the floor into lanes, so a fight is won by choosing which lane to be in rather than by out-shooting someone across an open room.
Ammunition is plentiful enough that suppressing a stairway or lane is a reasonable use of it, which is not true on the scarcer maps.
nuance.because: Library carries thirty-one AmmoBox records, the most of any arena.

nuance.claim: Because the map is played as movement between floors, the stairs and connections are far better mine placements than any room.
The long lanes between shelving suit precise weapons, so a player holding one end of a lane covers a great deal of the floor.
One-hit kills plus long lanes turn the map cautious; players hold angles rather than push, and the lower floor becomes the only comfortable place to move.
A carrier survives by changing floors repeatedly, using the enclosed lower area to break contact and the connections to stay ahead.
The marked holder should take the enclosed lower area, where the three hunters have to arrive one at a time through known entrances.
This is the most densely furnished of the dedicated arenas, which is why it supports four players without feeling cramped and why two-player matches on it drag.
nuance.because: Library carries seventy-one prop records against Basement's twenty-one, the widest spread among the arenas.
